slides.text: The house of the future opened in 1957, and in 1967 the wrecking ball bounced off it.
Monsanto paid for it and two MIT architects, Marvin Goody and Richard Hamilton, designed it: four plastic wings cantilevered off a concrete core.
Inside, it was set in 1986, with a microwave oven in the kitchen.
More than 20 million people walked through the house in its ten years.
When Tomorrowland was redone in 1967, the wrecking ball could not break the glass-reinforced plastic.
Crews tried torches, chainsaws and jackhammers, then crushed it with choker chains. The steel bolts holding it down broke before the house did.
The concrete foundation is still there, painted green and used as a planter.
For the friend who grew up going to Disneyland.
slides.sub: The Future, Then — tomorrow as it used to look
